---

<a id="page-public-rules-characters-prior-experience-skills-glossary"></a>

## Skills Glossary

Every skill the prior-experience generator can grant, the dice roll that grants
it, and **what it does at the table**. Use this with [Skill Tracks](../skill-tracks)
to roll up a character's past by hand — exactly the way the app does it.

### What a skill does

A skill makes you better at one kind of task. When you attempt something a skill
covers:

> **Skill check:** roll **2d6 + the governing attribute's modifier + your skill
> level**, against a difficulty the GM sets. A natural 12 always succeeds; a
> natural 2 always fails. Untrained, you roll with the attribute modifier alone.

Skill level adds **+1 per level**, so a skill contributes:

| Level | I | II | III | IV | V | VI |
| ----- | - | -- | --- | -- | - | -- |
| Bonus | +1 | +2 | +3 | +4 | +5 | +6 |

**There is no cap** — on the level or on the bonus. The table simply stops
where the page runs out of room; level VII is +7 and so on.

Levels are bought with skill points, and every skill charges the same:
**level 1 costs 1 point, level 2 costs 2 more, level 3 costs 3 more**, and so
on. Reaching level N therefore costs **N(N+1)/2** points in total:

| Level | I | II | III | IV | V | VI |
| ----- | - | -- | --- | -- | - | -- |
| Cumulative cost | 1 | 3 | 6 | 10 | 15 | 21 |

**Exception:** the **Arcane** skill (True Magic) costs **double** — level 1
costs 2 points, level N costs 2×N more, so reaching level N costs **N(N+1)**
points in total.

(See [Prior Experience](../../prior-experience) for where the points come
from.) A level V skill (+5) is worth as much as a peak attribute, and climbing
past it costs steeply but is never barred — so specializing matters. The
**Governs** column below names the attribute whose modifier the skill rides on;
the GM may substitute a better-fit attribute for an unusual use.

### Naming and renaming a skill

A skill's name says which rule it falls under, and renaming one never moves its
points to another skill. You make two choices by name: the craft of a **Maker
Skill** (once), and a **Village** origin's Street Smarts or Survival. Focusing
a **Knowledge** on a field is the GM's to allow. A **Weapon** skill is tied to its weapon the same
way — *Weapon (Broadsword)* — see [Weapon Classes](#weapon-classes). Moving
points from one skill to another is the GM's call alone.

### How a skill is granted

Each **year** in a track, **roll 1d20**; the result (1–20) is the position in
your track's list — that's the skill you gain. Roll a skill you already have and
the point goes toward its next level. Buy as many years as you like, one at a
time or in a run. See [Skill Tracks](../skill-tracks).

The **Rolled on** column lists every track and the d20 value(s) that grant the
skill. Read *Merchant 3* as "on the Merchant track, a roll of 3 grants it";
*Magic 14, 15* means a 14 or 15 on the Magic track. Track names are spelled out
in full.

### Combat skills

| Skill | Governs | Rolled on | What it does |
| ----- | ------- | --------- | ------------ |
| Weapon | DEX | Merchant 1 · Campaigner 2, 4, 6 · Laborer 1 · Underworld 1, 3 · Civil Service 1 · Craft 1 · Hunter/Gatherer 1, 3 | Taken for one **specific weapon**. Adds your full skill level to attacks with that weapon, and **half (rounded down)** with any other weapon of the same class (Unusual weapons excepted). See [Weapon Classes](#weapon-classes). |
| Weapon Parry | DEX | Merchant 2 · Campaigner 1, 3, 5, 7 · Laborer 2 · Underworld 2, 4 · Craft 2 · Hunter/Gatherer 2, 4 | Adds to your defense roll when parrying a melee attack with a weapon. |
| Archery | DEX | Hunter/Gatherer 5, 6, 7 | Adds to ranged attack rolls with bows, crossbows, and slings (the two Missile classes). |
| Poison | INT | Underworld 15 · Hunter/Gatherer 16 | Adds to rolls to brew, coat, and safely apply poisons (and to recognize them). |

### Social & roguish skills

| Skill | Governs | Rolled on | What it does |
| ----- | ------- | --------- | ------------ |
| Deceit | CHA | Merchant 4 · Magic 1 · Underworld 5 · Civil Service 2 | Adds to a sustained lie or con — a false identity, a forged story held over time. Opposed by the target's Detect Truth or WIS. |
| Bluff | CHA | Merchant 18 · Magic 16 · Underworld 17 | Adds to a quick, in-the-moment misdirection — fast talk, a feint, brazening past a guard. (Deceit is the long game; Bluff is the snap moment.) |
| Persuasion | CHA | Merchant 5 · Magic 2 · Underworld 6, 7 · Civil Service 3 | Adds to swaying one person by honest argument or appeal. |
| Diplomacy | CHA | Merchant 11 · Magic 17 · Underworld 18 · Civil Service 9 | Adds to formal negotiation, etiquette, and dealings between factions or before a court. |
| Detect Truth | WIS | Civil Service 4, 5 | Adds to reading sincerity and catching lies; opposes Deceit and Bluff. |
| Sleight of Hand | DEX | Merchant 6 · Magic 5 · Underworld 11 · Civil Service 20 | Adds to pickpocketing, palming, planting, and concealing small objects. |
| Stealth | DEX | Campaigner 17 · Underworld 10 · Hunter/Gatherer 17 | Adds to moving unseen and unheard; opposed by Perception or Alert. |
| Street Smarts | WIS | Merchant 8 · Underworld 9 · Civil Service 19 · Craft 19 | Adds to reading a city, finding the right people, and not getting played. |
| Bribery | CHA | Merchant 14 · Underworld 12 · Civil Service 12 | Adds to offering a bribe without giving offense and judging the right price. |
| Gamble | INT | Laborer 16 · Underworld 16 | Adds to games of chance and to spotting a cheat. |
| Morale | CHA | Merchant 10 | Adds to rallying allies, inspiring a crowd, and holding the line under fear. |
| Luck | — | Merchant 19 · Laborer 19 | **Special:** once per session per level, after seeing a roll's result you may add this skill's level to it. Governed by no attribute. |

### Trade, knowledge & craft skills

| Skill | Governs | Rolled on | What it does |
| ----- | ------- | --------- | ------------ |
| Coins | INT | Merchant 3 · Campaigner 11 · Laborer 3 · Magic 11 · Underworld 19 · Civil Service 13, 14 · Craft 12 | Adds to handling money: changing currency, judging a deal's finances, spotting counterfeit coin. |
| Barter | CHA | Merchant 13 · Campaigner 18 · Civil Service 11 · Craft 20 | Adds to haggling a better price in trade. |
| Appraise | INT | Merchant 15 · Underworld 13 · Civil Service 18 · Craft 10, 18 | Adds to judging the value, quality, and authenticity of goods. (Absorbs the former "Estimate".) |
| Logistics | INT | Merchant 12 · Civil Service 10 · Craft 9 | Adds to organizing supply, transport, and provisioning for a group or journey. |
| Literacy | INT | Merchant 7 · Campaigner 12 · Laborer 4 · Magic 3, 4 · Underworld 8 · Civil Service 15, 16 · Craft 8 | Lets you read and write; adds to deciphering or composing documents. Without it, you cannot read at all. |
| Knowledge | INT | Merchant 17 · Campaigner 13 · Laborer 5 · Magic 14, 15 · Civil Service 6, 7 · Craft 11 · Hunter/Gatherer 12 | Adds to recalling lore, history, and facts. (Taken broadly; the GM may let you focus a field for a larger bonus in it. A focused field is written after the skill, *Knowledge (History)*.) |
| Contracts/Law | INT | Civil Service 17 | Adds to legal procedure, contracts, and statute. |
| Maker Skill | INT | Laborer 6, 7 · Craft 13, 14, 15, 16, 17 | A **chosen craft** (smith, carpenter, tailor…), written after the skill: *Maker Skill (Smith)*. Adds to making and repairing in that craft; drives the Craft track's income. |
| Arts | CHA | Craft 5 | Adds to performing and creating fine art — music, painting, sculpture — and to judging it. |
| Enchanting | INT | Magic 18, 19 · Craft 3, 4 | Adds to imbuing items with magic and crafting magic items. |

**House ruling (provisional) on Literacy** — coordinator's ruling under the
standing rule; Spencer may overrule. The Literacy row above and the
[literacy check](../../location) ("the check to be literate at all, and is
separate from the Literacy skill") disagree. Until Spencer rules: *whether*
you can read at all is the literacy check your origin sets; a literate
character without the Literacy skill reads and writes untrained, and one who
failed the check cannot read, whatever this skill's level.

**House ruling (provisional) on a focused Knowledge field** — coordinator's
ruling under the standing rule; Spencer may overrule. The "larger bonus" a
focused field gives is **+1** to checks in that field, on top of the skill's
level. A focused field is the GM's to allow.

### Wilderness, survival & labor skills

| Skill | Governs | Rolled on | What it does |
| ----- | ------- | --------- | ------------ |
| Tracker | WIS | Campaigner 8 · Hunter/Gatherer 8, 9 | Adds to following tracks and reading sign. |
| Hunting | WIS | Campaigner 10 · Hunter/Gatherer 19, 20 | Adds to finding, stalking, and taking game. (Absorbs the former "Hunter".) |
| Survival | WIS | Campaigner 20 · Hunter/Gatherer 13 | Adds to finding food, water, and shelter and enduring exposure in the wild. |
| Weather/Path | WIS | Merchant 9 · Campaigner 19 · Civil Service 8 | Adds to predicting weather and finding or keeping an overland route (navigation). |
| Herb Lore | INT | Laborer 20 · Magic 13 · Craft 6, 7 · Hunter/Gatherer 10, 11 | Adds to identifying, gathering, and using herbs and their effects. (Absorbs the former "Herbs".) |
| Medic | INT | Campaigner 9 · Magic 12 | Adds to first aid, field healing, and stabilizing the dying. |
| Perception | INT | Merchant 16 · Campaigner 16 · Magic 6 · Underworld 14 · Hunter/Gatherer 18 | Adds to actively noticing and searching for hidden things. |
| Alert | WIS | Merchant 20 · Campaigner 14, 15 · Magic 20 · Underworld 20 · Hunter/Gatherer 14, 15 | Adds to avoiding surprise and to your reaction when ambushed. (Perception is looking *for* something; Alert is not being caught off guard.) |
| Portage | STR | Laborer 8, 9 | Adds to hauling heavy loads over distance and to feats of sustained carrying. |
| Miner | STR | Laborer 17 | Adds to mining, assessing ore, and working stone underground. |
| Sailor | DEX | Laborer 18 | Adds to crewing and sailing a ship and reading the sea. |

### Special / mechanical entries

These are not skill checks — they change the character sheet directly.

| Entry | Rolled on | Effect |
| ----- | --------- | ------ |
| +1 STR | Laborer 10, 13 | Permanently raises Strength by 1 (capped at the attribute max, 30). |
| +1 DEX | Laborer 11, 14 | Permanently raises Dexterity by 1 (capped). |
| +1 CON | Laborer 12, 15 | Permanently raises Constitution by 1 (capped). |
| Skill Point | Magic 7 | Adds 1 free skill point to spend anywhere. |
| Spell Point | Magic 8, 9, 10 | Magic fuel toward your **Mana Pool** — the resource spells are cast from (see the [Magic](../../../magic/casting-spells) rules) — tracked separately from skill points. |

### Weapon Classes

When you gain the **Weapon** skill, tie it to one specific weapon. You add your
**full** skill level to attacks with that exact weapon, and **half your level
(rounded down)** to attacks with any other weapon of the **same class**. A
weapon of a different class gets no bonus from that skill.

*Example:* Weapon (Broadsword) at Level IV gives **+4** with a broadsword and
**+2** with any other Striking weapon — a mace, a war ax, a saber.

**Unusual weapons are the exception:** they are too unlike one another to share
training, so each requires its **own** Weapon skill. A skill tied to an Unusual
weapon — quarterstaff, net, cestus, whip, lasso, boomerang, nunchaku, bola,
torch — gives its full level with that exact weapon and transfers **nothing**
in either direction, even with a weapon that shares its class below.

Weapons are grouped by **how their attack defeats armour**, not by shape, and
the classes are exactly the ones the [attack-roll Target Number
matrix](../../../combat/action-options/attack-rolls) uses — one source of
truth. Every catalog weapon carries its class in the `weapon_class` field:

| Class | Includes |
| ----- | -------- |
| Piercing | dagger, rapier |
| Striking | saber, shortsword, broadsword, bastard sword (1 hand), club, hatchet, hammer, mace, small ax, war ax, morningstar, quarterstaff, cestus, nunchaku, torch |
| Thrusting | javelin, spear, trident |
| Heavy Striking | bastard sword (2 hands), 2-handed sword, great sword, great hammer, battle axe |
| Heavy Thrusting | halberd, pike ax, pike, cavalry lance |
| Missile — Bows | sling, small bow, horse bow, longbow, thrown rock, boomerang |
| Missile — Crossbows | light crossbow, heavy crossbow |
| Flexible / Snare | whip, net, lasso, bola |

(Ammunition is not a weapon and has no class.)

**Archery** is, in effect, the Weapon skill for shooting — use it for ranged
attacks across both Missile classes.

### Open design questions

One entry still needs a ruling from the author:

- **Knowledge** — decide whether it stays broad or is taken as a chosen field.

Recently resolved: Luck (add your level to a roll after seeing it, once per
session per level); Spell Point (now its own pool); Jack of Trades (removed —
a d20 could never reach it).

### Manual roll-up in brief

1. Pick a [track](../skill-tracks). Start at age 16, level 1.
2. For each year: roll **1d20** → take that position's skill; make the
   **3d6 + best modifier** [survival roll](../survivability) (natural 18
   lives, natural 3 dies); add the track's XP and money; age 1 year.
3. Repeat for as many years as you want. From age 36 on, apply
   [aging](../aging) penalties as each four-year step is reached.
4. Convert total XP to skill points using the table in
   [Prior Experience](../../prior-experience), then spend them.

---

<a id="page-public-rules-magic"></a>

## Magic

### Mana Pool

Every character has a Mana Pool, built from the **Spell Points** earned through training in the Magic skill track. It starts at 0 and grows only with the Spell Points the Magic track grants (a roll of 8, 9 or 10 on its d20) — ordinary skill points do not convert into mana — and a Game Master may grant mana. There is no roll at character creation, and the total is **visible**: you always know your exact Pool.

Spells themselves are learned with skill points: see [Spell Mastery](spell-mastery). Level I in a spell lets you cast it, paying mana equal to the spell's level.

Mana is completely separate from other attributes. A clever weakling may have vast magical reserves; a brilliant scholar may have almost none.

---

<a id="page-public-rules-magic-casting-spells"></a>

## Casting Spells

**Cost:** Spells cost mana equal to the spell's level.

**Roll:** 3d6 ≤ INT or WIS (depending on the spell)

Very low and very high rolls have special effects—some fortunate, some catastrophic. Your GM will tell you what happens.

**Some spells must hit:** Magic requiring hitting a target needs an additional DEX roll.

### Renewing Spells

Continuing spells require mana payment each turn during Phase 2 of combat. Unrenewed spells end immediately.

---

<a id="page-public-rules-magic-spell-mastery"></a>

## Spell Mastery

Multiple skill points in a spell grant additional abilities:

| Level | Benefit                                                                              |
| ----- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| 1     | Can cast the spell                                                                   |
| 2     | Cast without hand gestures                                                           |
| 3     | Cast without verbal incantation; unlocks protection from same spell (separate skill) |
| 4     | Reduced mana cost; unlocks halt same spell (separate skill)                          |
| 5     | Further reduced cost; unlocks reflect same spell back onto caster (separate skill)   |

---

<a id="page-public-rules-magic-push-boosting"></a>

## Push (Boosting)

Casters can invest additional mana beyond base cost for greater effect. This is dangerous.

The more mana you channel, the harder it becomes to maintain control. Pushing requires a **Control Roll** (3d6 ≤ INT), and the penalty grows with the power you're attempting to wield.

Fail badly enough—or roll an 18—and the magic slips your grasp entirely. This is called **Runaway**.

### Borrowing

When you don't have enough mana, you can attempt to Borrow—drawing on reserves you may not have. This creates Debt, and Debt must be paid. The deeper the Debt, the more likely something goes wrong.

---

<a id="page-public-rules-magic-runaway"></a>

## Runaway

When magic slips from control, it feeds on the caster.

The experience is terrifying. The spell destabilizes. You feel your reserves draining away—first your mana, then your very life force. Blood runs from your nose, your eyes. Each moment you struggle to regain control, and each moment the task grows harder.

Those who survive Runaway often bear permanent marks: white streaks in their hair, strange scars, a haunted look. Those who don't survive… the kindest outcome is a quick death.

**Anchor Roll:** Each round, you attempt to regain control by rolling 3d6 ≤ WIS.

When your Pool empties, you fall unconscious, and the magic begins consuming your Body instead. When your Body fails, you die.

### Intervention

Another mage can attempt to help a caster caught in Runaway—but this is not without risk. If the intervention fails, both mages are caught in the magical maelstrom.

Those who intervene successfully earn deep gratitude. Those who try and fail… well, at least they tried.

---

<a id="page-public-rules-magic-counterspell"></a>

## Counterspell

Mages can attempt to counter enemy spells by investing their own mana and engaging in a contest of will. The defender commits mana and both roll opposed INT checks—the more mana invested, the better your chances.

If the defender wins, the spell is countered. If the caster wins, the spell goes through—but the caster may attempt again next turn, escalating the duel. Only the caster can escalate; the defender gets one chance to stop each casting.

These duels can drain both parties quickly, and a failed Control Roll during escalation can trigger Runaway.

---

<a id="page-public-rules-magic-schools-of-magic"></a>

## Schools of Magic

### Common Schools (0-70%)

- Elemental (water, fire, lightning, earth, wind)
- Passage
- Protection
- Mending

### Less Common Schools (71-100%)

- Weather
- Counter
- Arcane/True Magic
- Control

### Spell Lists

#### Elemental

1. Missile
2. Ball
3. Bolt
4. Shield
5. Barrier
6. Elemental

#### Passage

1. Detect Magic, Light
2. Knock, Hold, Blur
3. Transparency, Detect Invisibility, Lock
4. Breathing
5. Flying
6. Pass Wall
7. Shape Change

#### Protection

1. Counter 1, Shield, Detect Magic
2. Counter 2, Shield Wall, Knowledge
3. Counter 3, Minor Protection from Element
4. Counter 4, Major Protection from Element
5. Counter 5, Encase

#### Mending

1. Heal
2. Cure
3. Web/Joining, Breaking
4. Shaping

#### Weather

1. Detect Weather
2. Wind, Wind Counter
3. Rain, Rain Counter
4. Storm, Storm Counter

#### Control

1. Persuade Minor, Calm, Enrage
2. Minor Illusion (including Blur), Fatigue
3. Wound, Effect Mental State/Senses (Sleep, Confusion, Blind, Deafen, Laugh)
4. Persuade Major, Illusion (including Transparency)
5. Major Illusion, Area Effect, Effect Senses
6. Force (Paralyze, Move, Breath, Run, Sleep, etc.)

---

<a id="page-public-rules-magic-spell-descriptions"></a>

## Spell Descriptions

Every spell in the [Schools of Magic](../schools-of-magic) list, described, with
the attribute that matters most when you cast it.

**Reading the tables:** *Lvl* is the spell's tier within its school, and per
[Casting Spells](../casting-spells) it's also the **mana cost** — a level 4
spell costs 4 mana to cast. *Affinity* is whichever of INT or WIS the
[Casting Roll](../casting-spells) uses for that spell (3d6 ≤ your attribute);
*Why* is a one-line reason, not a house rule — your GM has final say on any
spell not listed here.

**The general split:** INT governs spells that require precise technical
control — shaping raw force, working a mechanism, crafting a false
sense-impression exactly. WIS governs spells that call on judgment,
insight, or endurance — reading a mind, reading the weather, sensing what a
wound or a threat needs. Most schools lean one way; a few split spell by
spell.

### Elemental

Common school. Every spell below can be cast in any of the five elemental
flavors — **water, fire, lightning, earth, wind** — chosen when you learn
it; a caster who wants more than one flavor of the same spell learns it
again. All Elemental spells are **INT**: shaping a bolt of flame or a wall
of stone into an exact form is technique, not insight.

| Spell | Lvl | Affinity | Why | Description |
| ----- | --- | -------- | --- | ------------ |
| Missile | 1 | INT | Precise single-target force needs technical control. | A small, fast dart of your chosen element, flung at one target. The bread-and-butter attack spell — cheap, quick to cast, and (per [Casting Spells](../casting-spells)) needs a hit roll on top of the casting roll, since it has to land as well as form. |
| Ball | 2 | INT | Same technique, shaped to spread instead of pierce. | A globe of your element that expands to strike everyone in a small area, not just one target. Costs more to hold its shape as it grows — friendly fire is a real risk in a tight formation. |
| Bolt | 3 | INT | A stronger, single-line application of the same control. | A punishing line of your element, faster and harder-hitting than a Missile, still aimed at one target or in a line through several. The step up in level buys raw power, not new tricks. |
| Shield (Elemental) | 4 | INT | Holding a precise, constantly-adjusting ward around yourself. | A personal ward that dampens or deflects incoming attacks of the caster's chosen element. It has to track and cancel force in real time, which is why it costs more than the offensive spells beneath it. Distinct from Protection's **Shield**, below — this one only stops its own element. |
| Barrier | 5 | INT | Shaping a standing, lasting structure out of raw element. | A wall or dome of the chosen element, large enough to block movement and line of sight, or to box enemies in. Holds its shape without the caster's continued attention once it's up, though it still needs renewal to persist past the turn it's cast. |
| Elemental | 6 | INT | The school's capstone: total command of the medium. | The full expression of the school — a lasting, powerful manifestation of the caster's element, closer to summoning a localized force of nature than throwing a spell. GMs should treat its exact effect as a set-piece, not a fixed stat block. |

### Passage

Common school. Detection, access, and movement magic — mostly technical
alteration of physical reality, which is why it stays **INT** almost
straight down the list.

| Spell | Lvl | Affinity | Why | Description |
| ----- | --- | -------- | --- | ------------ |
| Detect Magic | 1 | INT | Reading a trace of worked power is perception, not judgment. | Reveals whether magic has touched an object, place, or person nearby — not what it does, just that it's there. Also appears in Protection's spell list at the same level; it's one spell, learnable from either track. |
| Light | 1 | INT | A simple, exact technical effect. | Conjures a small, steady light source at a point the caster designates — no heat, no fuel, no flicker. The first spell most casters ever learn. |
| Knock | 2 | INT | Forcing a mechanism is a technical problem. | Pops a mundane lock or latch without a key, working the mechanism from a distance rather than breaking it. Wards and magical locks resist it; ordinary ones rarely do. |
| Hold | 2 | INT | Precisely pinning an object or door in place. | Fixes a door, object, or small structure so it cannot be opened, moved, or forced by ordinary means until the spell lapses or is countered. |
| Blur | 2 | INT | Crafting an exact false sense-impression. | Smears the caster's outline just enough to spoil an attacker's aim — treat it as the caster's own dodge trick, not true invisibility. Referenced again, thematically, under Control's Minor Illusion, which produces a similar look through a different school. |
| Transparency | 3 | INT | A harder, more precise version of the same trick. | Renders the target (self or another) invisible or see-through for the duration — a full step up from Blur's mere distortion. Control's **Illusion** spell can mimic the effect on someone else's target, at a higher level and less reliably. |
| Detect Invisibility | 3 | INT | Perception again — seeing through a technique, not judging intent. | Lets the caster see anything hidden by invisibility or similar concealment magic for the duration, including the caster's own Transparency countered against them. |
| Lock | 3 | INT | The offensive twin of Knock: precisely jamming a mechanism. | Seals a mundane lock, latch, or door shut against anyone but the caster — the reverse of Knock, and just as easily countered by a rival caster's Knock. |
| Breathing | 4 | INT | Sustaining an exact physical condition around the body. | Lets the target breathe normally underwater, in smoke, or in thin air for the duration — a precise, sustained alteration of the air immediately around them rather than a change to their body. |
| Flying | 5 | INT | Continuous, exacting control over the target's own momentum. | Grants the target true, controlled flight for the duration. High-cost and high-value: it turns the vertical axis and any water or chasm into a non-obstacle, which is exactly why it sits near the top of the school. |
| Pass Wall | 6 | INT | Precisely unmaking a solid barrier for a moment. | Opens a temporary passage straight through a wall or similar solid barrier, closing again once the spell ends (with anyone still inside when it closes at the GM's mercy). |
| Shape Change | 7 | INT | The school's capstone: total technical control of one's own form. | Reshapes the caster's own body into another form — animal, or something stranger — for the duration. The highest-level Passage spell for a reason: getting every detail of an unfamiliar body right, and getting back, is exacting work. |

### Protection

Common school. Warding and defensive magic — instinct and judgment about
what's coming, which puts most of it on the **WIS** side of the split.

| Spell | Lvl | Affinity | Why | Description |
| ----- | --- | -------- | --- | ------------ |
| Counter | 1–5 | WIS | Reading an opposing caster's intent and will, not shaping force. | Invests mana to oppose an enemy spell as it's cast — this is the spell version of the [Counterspell](../counterspell) duel: commit mana, roll opposed against the attacker, and win or lose the contest. Its five tiers are the five levels of investment a caster can bring to that duel, not five different spells. |
| Shield (Protection) | 1 | WIS | A defensive instinct, not a shaped effect. | A general ward that improves the target's chances against an incoming attack (mundane or magical) rather than blocking one element specifically. Where Elemental's **Shield** is a precise dampening field, this one is closer to a heightened sense of danger made physical. |
| Detect Magic | 1 | INT | Reading a trace of worked power is perception, not judgment. | See Passage, above — the same spell, taught on this track as well. |
| Shield Wall | 2 | WIS | Extending protective instinct to a group. | Extends a Shield-like ward across a line of allies rather than a single target — a formation spell, cast by whoever is standing where the enemy will hit hardest. |
| Knowledge | 2 | WIS | Insight and judgment about what's known, not a technical readout. | Surfaces relevant facts the caster (or a target) doesn't consciously know, at the GM's discretion — closer to a flash of applied wisdom than a spell-as-search-engine. |
| Minor Protection from Element | 3 | WIS | Judging and blunting a specific danger. | Grants meaningful resistance to one element (fire, cold, and so on) for the duration — the practical answer to Elemental's offensive spells. |
| Major Protection from Element | 4 | WIS | The stronger form of the same protective judgment. | As Minor Protection, but the resistance is much harder to overcome — the answer to a caster who's learned Barrier or Elemental in that same element. |
| Encase | 5 | WIS | A defensive judgment call taken to its extreme: total isolation. | Seals the target (willing or not) inside a nearly impenetrable shell — the strongest single-target defense in the school, and a favorite for containing something dangerous rather than protecting an ally. |

### Mending

Common school. Healing and repair — sensing what a body or an object needs
to be whole, which is **WIS**'s domain even though the mundane Medic
skill
that does similar work is INT-governed. The skill is trained clinical
technique; the spell is closer to a felt sense of what's wrong.

| Spell | Lvl | Affinity | Why | Description |
| ----- | --- | -------- | --- | ------------ |
| Heal | 1 | WIS | Sensing and closing a wound is insight, not force. | Restores Fatigue (and, on a strong casting roll, some Body) to the target — the school's foundation spell and the most commonly known spell in Tarmar for exactly that reason. |
| Cure | 2 | WIS | Judging what's poisoning or afflicting the body. | Removes poison, disease, or a similar ongoing affliction from the target, rather than restoring points directly the way Heal does. |
| Web/Joining | 3 | WIS | Sensing where two things belong together. | Binds a target in place with sticky, rope-like strands (Web), or fuses two broken pieces of an object or wound edge back together (Joining) — two applications of the same "make things adhere" principle, one hostile, one restorative. |
| Breaking | 3 | WIS | The inverse judgment: sensing a structure's weak point. | Weakens or shatters an object's structural integrity at a chosen point — Web/Joining's opposite number, aimed at things rather than people. |
| Shaping | 4 | WIS | The school's capstone: full sculptural insight into material. | Reshapes an existing quantity of material (stone, wood, metal, flesh) into a new form the caster has in mind, gradually rather than instantly — closer to expert sculpture than teleportation-of-matter. |

### Weather

Less common school (71–100%). Reading and, eventually, bending the sky —
**WIS** all the way through, matching the mundane Weather/Path
skill's
own WIS governance.

| Spell | Lvl | Affinity | Why | Description |
| ----- | --- | -------- | --- | ------------ |
| Detect Weather | 1 | WIS | Reading the sky is awareness and judgment. | Tells the caster what weather is coming over the next short while — the entry point to the school and a staple for anyone who sails or campaigns by it. |
| Wind | 2 | WIS | Calling weather is an extension of reading it. | Raises or redirects a local wind — enough to fill a sail, scatter smoke, or spoil an archer's aim. |
| Wind Counter | 2 | WIS | Judging and canceling an opposing pattern. | Cancels or calms an existing wind effect, mundane or magical — Wind's opposite number. |
| Rain | 3 | WIS | A stronger application of the same weather-sense. | Calls rain over an area — useful for dousing fire, ruining a pursuer's tracks, or simply making everyone miserable. |
| Rain Counter | 3 | WIS | Judging and clearing an opposing pattern. | Clears rain, mundane or conjured, from the area — Rain's opposite number. |
| Storm | 4 | WIS | The strongest weather-calling the school offers. | Summons a genuine storm — heavy rain or snow, high wind, and reduced visibility over a real area, not just around the caster. |
| Storm Counter | 4 | WIS | The strongest weather-canceling judgment the school offers. | Breaks an existing storm, mundane or conjured — Storm's opposite number and the top of the school. |

### Control

Less common school. Splits down the middle: spells that work on a mind
(insight, so **WIS**) versus spells that work through a crafted false
sense-impression or raw compulsion (technique, so **INT**).

| Spell | Lvl | Affinity | Why | Description |
| ----- | --- | -------- | --- | ------------ |
| Persuade Minor | 1 | WIS | Reading a mind well enough to nudge it. | Makes a suggestion feel more reasonable to the target than it otherwise would — a magical thumb on the scale of an ordinary conversation, not mind control. |
| Calm | 1 | WIS | Judging and settling a target's emotional state. | Soothes a frightened, enraged, or panicking target toward a level head. Works on crowds as easily as individuals, which makes it a favorite for riot control. |
| Enrage | 1 | WIS | The same insight, aimed the other direction. | Calm's opposite number: pushes a target toward anger or aggression, useful for turning a calm negotiation hostile or a wavering line into a charge. |
| Minor Illusion | 2 | INT | Crafting a false sense-impression is exacting technique. | Produces a small false sight, sound, or sensation — a flicker, a whisper, a shape at the edge of vision. Covers effects in the spirit of Passage's **Blur**, though built through a different school and less durable than a dedicated Passage spell. |
| Fatigue | 2 | INT | A direct, technical drain, closer to a weapon than a mind-effect. | Saps the target's Fatigue points directly, the spell-equivalent of exhausting someone through pure magical force rather than a blow. |
| Wound | 3 | INT | A direct, technical drain reaching further than Fatigue. | As Fatigue, but hits harder and can reach Body as well — the school's answer to a straightforward damage spell. |
| Effect Mental State/Senses | 3 | WIS | Reading a mind precisely enough to override one of its senses or states. | A family of single-effect spells at this level: **Sleep**, **Confusion**, **Blind**, **Deafen**, **Laugh** — each imposes exactly what it says on the target's mind or senses for the duration. The caster learns them individually; treat each as level 3. |
| Persuade Major | 4 | WIS | The stronger form of the same mind-reading judgment. | As Persuade Minor, but the suggestion can run against the target's own interests and still land, given a strong enough casting roll. |
| Illusion | 4 | INT | A larger, more convincing crafted sense-impression. | Produces a more complete and durable false sight or sound than Minor Illusion — a real phantom rather than a flicker. Can approximate Passage's **Transparency** on an unwilling target, at the cost of a higher level and less certainty. |
| Major Illusion | 5 | INT | The strongest single-sense illusion the school offers. | A large, detailed, and durable illusion, potentially fooling more than one sense at once and holding up to real scrutiny far longer than Illusion. |
| Area Effect | 5 | INT | Extending precise sensory craft across a whole area. | Not a single effect but a modifier: lets the caster spread another Control illusion or sense-effect across an area rather than a single target — usually paired with Illusion or Major Illusion. |
| Effect Senses | 5 | INT | Directly overriding a target's senses is technical, not persuasive. | Blocks, dulls, or falsifies one of the target's senses outright (beyond the specific Blind/Deafen pair at level 3) — a broader, higher-level sensory override. |
| Force | 6 | INT | Raw compulsion of a body against its will is pure technique. | The school's capstone: a family of effects — **Paralyze**, **Move**, **Breath**, **Run**, **Sleep**, and others at the GM's discretion — that physically compel the target's body rather than persuading their mind. Each still costs a level-6 casting; a caster typically knows it for one or two named effects, not the whole family at once. |

### Open questions for the author

- **Element choice at character creation vs. per-spell:** whether a caster
  fixes one elemental flavor for their whole Elemental track or picks it
  spell-by-spell is left to the GM until ruled.
- **"Force …, etc." (Control 6):** the source list leaves this open-ended;
  treat Paralyze/Move/Breath/Run/Sleep as the known set and let the GM add
  more at the same level.

---

<a id="page-public-rules-combat"></a>

## Combat

### The Turn

A turn represents approximately **five seconds** of action. Nothing happens simultaneously--each movement and action can affect what follows.

---

<a id="page-public-rules-combat-turn-sequence"></a>

## Turn Sequence

| Phase | Name                 | Order                      | Description                                                |
| ----- | -------------------- | -------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------- |
| 1     | **Initiative**       | 1d6 + adjDEX per combatant | Descending total; ties: higher adjDEX, then stable order   |
| 2     | **Renew Spells**     | DEX+INT+WIS (high→low)     | Pay mana to maintain continuing spells                     |
| 3     | **Initial Movement** | Initiative order           | Move or yield; movement stops upon engagement              |
| 4     | **Final Movement**   | Initiative order           | Those who yielded now move                                 |
| 5     | **Actions**          | adjDEX (high→low)          | Execute chosen action                                      |
| 6     | **Forced Retreat**   | —                          | Those who dealt physical hits (damage past the armour) and took none may push enemies back |

Each combatant rolls their own initiative: 1d6 plus their adjDEX modifier,
rerolled every turn. Phases 3 and 4 run in descending order of that total;
a tie goes to the higher adjDEX, and any tie still standing keeps a stable
order. This supersedes the older side-based roll in which the winner chose
to move first or second — that tactical choice survives as yielding: any
combatant may hold their Initial Movement and move in Final Movement
instead.

---

<a id="page-public-rules-combat-action-options"></a>

## Action Options

### Disengaged Figures

| Option | Name           | Move         | Action                                            |
| ------ | -------------- | ------------ | ------------------------------------------------- |
| a      | MOVE           | Run/Sprint   | None (movement only). Fatigue per gait            |
| b      | CHARGE ATTACK  | Jog or less  | Melee attack or HTH                               |
| c      | DODGE          | Jog or less  | +4 to your Target Number (missiles/thrown/missile spells) |
| d      | DROP           | Jog or less  | Go prone or kneeling                              |
| e      | READY WEAPON   | Walk         | Re-sling current, ready new weapon/shield         |
| f      | MISSILE ATTACK | Walk (slow)  | Fire bow, crossbow, or thrown weapon              |
| g      | STAND UP       | 0            | Rise from prone/kneeling (entire turn)            |
|        | CRAWL          | 2 hex        | Move while prone (stay prone)                     |
| h      | CAST SPELL     | Walk (slow)  | Attempt any spell                                 |
| i      | DISBELIEVE     | Walk (slow)  | See through one illusion                          |

### Engaged Figures

| Option | Name           | Move        | Action                                     |
| ------ | -------------- | ----------- | ------------------------------------------ |
| j      | ATTACK         | Shift/still | Melee attack (non-missile)                 |
| k      | DEFEND         | Shift/still | +4 to your Target Number (melee/non-missile) |
| l      | ONE LAST SHOT  | Still       | Fire missile (if ready before engaged)     |
| m      | CHANGE WEAPON  | Shift/still | Drop current, ready new non-missile        |
| n      | DISENGAGE      | Shift/still | Move 1 hex any direction instead of attack |
| o      | ATTEMPT HTH    | Shift/still | Move INTO enemy hex, bare hands/dagger     |
| p      | STAND UP       | Still       | Rise from prone/kneeling (entire turn)     |
| q      | PICK UP WEAPON | Still       | Drop yours, grab from hex/adjacent         |
| r      | CAST SPELL     | Shift/still | Attempt any spell                          |
| s      | DISBELIEVE     | Shift/still | See through one illusion                   |

### Hand-to-Hand Combat

| Option | Name        | Action                                   |
| ------ | ----------- | ---------------------------------------- |
| t      | HTH ATTACK  | Bare hands or dagger. Both get +4 to hit |
| u      | DRAW DAGGER | Roll 3d6 ≤ DEX to ready dagger           |
| v      | DISENGAGE   | Roll 4d6 ≤ DEX → stand, move to adjacent |
|        | CAST SPELL  | If hands free or no-gesture spell        |

---

<a id="page-public-rules-combat-action-options-movement"></a>

## Movement

**Hex Size:** 5 feet (1.5 meters). Each movement phase is approximately 5 seconds.

**Megahex:** 7 hexes (1 center + 6 surrounding). Used for missile range.

*(image: Megahex diagram)*

**Movement Modifier:** CON modifier + STR modifier + DEX modifier

| Speed       | Distance (hexes) | Fatigue Cost                 | Available Actions               |
| ----------- | ---------------- | ---------------------------- | ------------------------------- |
| Sprint      | 18 + modifier    | 6 per turn                   | None                            |
| Run         | 12 + modifier    | 1 per turn                   | None                            |
| Jog         | 7 + modifier     | None (combat) / 1 per 10 min | Charge Attack, Dodge, Drop      |
| Walk        | 4 + modifier     | None                         | Ready Weapon                    |
| Walk (slow) | Up to 2 hex      | None                         | Cast Spell, Missile, Disbelieve |
| Stand Still | 0                | None                         | Stand Up, Pick Up Weapon        |

*Example: A character with CON 14 (+1), STR 10 (0), DEX 12 (0) has a movement modifier of +1. They walk 5, jog 8, run 13, sprint 19.*

### Encumbrance

Equipment weights are listed in pounds (lbs). For reference, 1 stone = 14 lbs. Based on weight carried compared to STR:

| Load Level   | Weight Carried     | Movement Penalty | Restrictions               |
| ------------ | ------------------ | ---------------- | -------------------------- |
| Unencumbered | Up to STR lbs      | 0                | —                          |
| Light        | STR+1 to STR×1.5   | −1               | —                          |
| Medium       | STR×1.5+1 to STR×2 | −2               | Cannot Run or Sprint       |
| Heavy        | STR×2+1 to STR×2.5 | −4               | Cannot Jog, Run, or Sprint |
| Overloaded   | Over STR×2.5       | —                | Walk only, 1 hex max       |

**Dropping a Pack:** Free action at start of movement. Picking up takes one full turn.

### Facing

Each figure faces one hex side, determining front, side, and rear hexes.

*(image: Facing diagram)*

- Physical attacks: Only into your front hexes
- Spells: Your hex, adjacent hexes, or any hex "in front"
- Prone/crawling: All hexes count as rear

### Engagement

| Figure Type    | Engaged When...                                       |
| -------------- | ----------------------------------------------------- |
| One-hex figure | In an armed enemy's front hex                         |
| 3–6 hex figure | In front hexes of 2+ one-hex figures (or 1 multi-hex) |
| 7-hex figure   | In front hexes of 3+ one-hex figures (or 1 multi-hex) |

Figures **stop immediately** when engaged.

---

<a id="page-public-rules-combat-action-options-attack-rolls"></a>

## Attack Rolls

Combat attacks use a **d20 roll-over**. Roll **1d20, add your to-hit bonus, and
compare to the Target Number (TN)**:

```
d20 + to-hit bonus ≥ Target Number  →  HIT
```

(Only combat attacks use the d20. A **skill check** rolls **2d6 + the
governing attribute's modifier + your skill level** against a difficulty the
GM sets, as the [Skills Glossary](../../../characters/prior-experience/skills-glossary)
defines it — that page is the source. An attribute check with no skill,
survival saves, and spellcasting still roll **3d6 ≤ attribute**.)

### To-Hit Bonus

Add these together:

| Source | Value |
| ------ | ----- |
| DEX combat modifier | `floor((effective DEX − 10) / 2)` — DEX 10 → +0, 14 → +2, 18 → +4 |
| Weapon skill | **+1 per skill level** with the weapon the skill was taken for, and **half your level (rounded down)** with another weapon of the same class (see below; Unusual weapons transfer nothing) |
| Under-strength penalty | −1 per point your effective STR is below the weapon's `str_req` (see below) |
| Situational modifiers | flanking, position, range, footing (see [[dex-adjustments]]) |

Effective DEX already has your armour's DEX penalty baked in, so heavy armour
drags down your aim as well as protecting you.

#### Weapon Skill

A **Weapon** skill is taken for one specific weapon, and each level of it is
worth **+1 to hit** with that weapon. There is **no cap** — on the level or on
the bonus. Level 3 in Weapon (Broadsword) is +3 with a broadsword; level 8 is
+8.

With **any other weapon of the same class** — the same classes the Target
Number matrix uses, below — the skill is worth **half your level, rounded
down**. Level 3 in Weapon (Broadsword), a Striking weapon, is therefore +1 with
a mace or a war ax. Against a weapon of a *different* class the skill does
nothing: broadsword training buys you no accuracy with a longbow.

**Unusual weapons** (quarterstaff, net, whip, lasso, and their kin) are the
exception: each needs its **own** Weapon skill, and no half-level transfer
applies in either direction — even between two Unusual weapons.

Levels are bought with skill points and cost the same for every skill (one
exception: **Arcane** costs double — see the glossary): **level 1
costs 1 point, level 2 costs 2 more, level 3 costs 3 more**, and so on — so
reaching level N costs **N(N+1)/2** points in total (1, 3, 6, 10, 15, 21, …).
See [Skills Glossary](../../../characters/prior-experience/skills-glossary).

#### Wielding a Weapon You're Too Weak For

You can **always** swing a weapon you lack the strength for — you just do it
badly. If your effective STR is below the weapon's `str_req`, take a to-hit
penalty equal to the shortfall: **−1 per point under**.

`STR-fit penalty = min(0, effective STR − str_req)`

Examples: STR 12 with a weapon needing 12 → no penalty. STR 12 with one needing
14 → **−2 to hit**. STR 10 with one needing 15 → **−5 to hit**. Strength buys
*access*, not accuracy — exceeding the requirement gives no bonus.

### Target Number

```
TN = base TN (weapon-class × armour-tier matrix, below)
   + shield bonus
   + defender's DEX-dodge modifier
```

The base difficulty comes entirely from **how your weapon's attack motion fares
against the defender's armour** — not from DEX. DEX only feeds your aim (above)
and the defender's dodge.

- **Defender's DEX-dodge** = `floor((defender effective DEX − 10) / 2)`, minimum 0.
- **Shield bonus** (added to TN): small/spike shield +1, large shield +2,
  tower shield +3, main-gauche +1 (parry).

#### Weapon Classes

Weapons are grouped by how their attack defeats armour, not by shape:

- **Piercing** — light quick points (dagger, rapier): brutal on the soft, futile on plate.
- **Striking** — one-handed cuts/blunt (broadsword, mace, club): even across all armour.
- **Thrusting** — braced/reach points (spear, trident): good vs medium, fades vs heavy.
- **Heavy Striking** — two-handed crush/cleave (great sword, great hammer, battle axe): high floor, but momentum cracks plate.
- **Heavy Thrusting** — braced polearms & lances (halberd, pike, lance): leverage punches through the heaviest armour.
- **Missile — Bows** — bows, slings, thrown: fade hard vs heavy armour.
- **Missile — Crossbows** — crossbows: flat vs armour, punch plate.
- **Flexible / Snare** — whip, net, lasso, bola: control weapons, poor vs anything rigid.

#### Armour Tiers

| Tier | Armour |
| ---- | ------ |
| None | unarmoured |
| Light | cloth, leather |
| Medium | chainmail |
| Heavy | half-plate, plate, fine plate |

#### Base Target Number Matrix

| Class | None | Light | Medium | Heavy |
| ----- | ---- | ----- | ------ | ----- |
| Piercing | 11 | 14 | 18 | 22 |
| Striking | 13 | 14 | 16 | 18 |
| Thrusting | 12 | 14 | 16 | 19 |
| Heavy Striking | 14 | 14 | 15 | 16 |
| Heavy Thrusting | 14 | 14 | 15 | 15 |
| Missile — Bows | 12 | 14 | 17 | 20 |
| Missile — Crossbows | 13 | 14 | 15 | 16 |
| Flexible / Snare | 13 | 16 | 19 | 22 |

A TN of 21–22 cannot be met on a raw die — a dagger against full plate (22) is
impossible without skill, a found gap (situational bonus), or a natural 20.

### Natural Rolls

- **Natural 20** → auto-hit regardless of TN, and a **critical**: roll the weapon's
  damage dice **twice**. Then **confirm** — roll a second d20 to-hit against the
  same TN; if it also hits, the blow is severe: **triple damage + bleeding**,
  reaching **Body** as well as Fatigue. The confirm uses the same TN with the
  same bonus, and its own naturals only decide the confirmation: a natural 1 on
  the confirm simply fails to confirm — it is not a second fumble — and a
  natural 20 confirms automatically.
- **Natural 1** → auto-miss, and a **fumble**. Roll 1d6: **1–3** off-balance (−2 to
  your next action) · **4–5** drop weapon · **6** weapon takes stress (breaks on a
  second fumble).

### Damage and Armour

Armour does **two jobs**: it raises the TN (above), *and* on a hit its `stops`
still subtract from damage.

```
damage = weapon dice + damage_mod − stops   (floored at 0)
```

**Exception (plate-cracking):** a **Heavy Striking** or **Heavy Thrusting** weapon
that beats a **Heavy**-armour target on the matrix ignores **half** the armour's
`stops` — the impact transfers through the plate.

Damage applies to **Fatigue** first; a severe crit reaches **Body** as well.

---

<a id="page-public-rules-combat-action-options-dex-adjustments"></a>

## Situational Modifiers

These are the old DEX adjustments, re-signed for the **d20 roll-over** system.
Each one now changes either the **attacker's to-hit total** (positive = easier)
or the **defender's Target Number** (see [[attack-rolls]]). All are cumulative.

### Positional Advantage (add to attacker's to-hit roll)

| Situation | To-hit |
| --------- | ------ |
| Striking from enemy's side hex | +2 |
| Striking from enemy's rear hex | +4 |
| Pole-weapon vs. charging opponent | +2 |
| Crossbow fired from prone | +1 |
| Waiting for an opening (1 turn) | +1 |
| Waiting for an opening (2+ turns) | +2 |
| HTH combat | +4 (both) |

### Target Conditions (subtract from attacker's to-hit roll)

| Condition | To-hit |
| --------- | ------ |
| Target is invisible | −6 |
| Target is in a shadow hex | −4 |
| Target is a one-hex figure in flight | −4 |
| Target is a giant snake | −3 |
| Target is a multi-hex figure in flight | −1 |

### Your Conditions (subtract from attacker's to-hit roll)

| Condition | To-hit |
| --------- | ------ |
| In shadow hex or firing through shadow | −6 |
| Two-weapon fighting | −4 on both |
| Sweeping blow (all 3 front hexes) | −4 |
| Standing in fire | −2 |
| Standing on a body | −2 |
| Moving over broken ground | −2 |

### Range (Thrown Weapons)

−1 to hit per hex to target.

### Range (Missile Weapons)

| Range (Megahexes) | To-hit |
| ----------------- | ------ |
| 0–2 MH | 0 |
| 3–4 MH | −1 |
| 5–6 MH | −2 |
| 7–8 MH | −3 |
| (continues) | −1 per 2 MH |

### Armour and Shields

Armour is no longer a flat to-hit adjustment — it is handled by the **weapon-class
× armour-tier matrix** that sets the base Target Number (see [[attack-rolls]]).
**Shields** add to the defender's Target Number instead:

| Shield | TN |
| ------ | -- |
| Small / spike shield | +1 |
| Large shield | +2 |
| Tower shield | +3 |
| Main-gauche (parry) | +1 |

---

<a id="page-public-rules-combat-action-options-special-combat-situations"></a>

## Special Combat Situations

### Disengaging

**From Engaged (option n):**
- Shift 1 hex or stand still during movement
- Move 1 hex any direction instead of attacking
- Faster enemies (higher adjDEX) can still strike
- Slower enemies attack at penalty = difference in adjDEX

**From HTH (option v):**
- Roll 4d6 ≤ DEX
- Success: stand up and move to adjacent empty hex
- Failure: remain in HTH

### Hand-to-Hand Combat

A figure may enter an enemy's hex if:
- Enemy has back to wall
- Enemy is down, prone, or kneeling
- Enemy has lower movement modifier
- Attacker comes from rear
- Enemy agrees

**Both combatants get +4 DEX adjustment.**

#### Bare-Handed Damage by STR

| STR       | Damage | STR   | Damage |
| --------- | ------ | ----- | ------ |
| 8 or less | 1d6−4  | 17–20 | 1d6+1  |
| 9–10      | 1d6−3  | 21–24 | 1d6+2  |
| 11–12     | 1d6−2  | 25–30 | 1d6+3  |
| 13–14     | 1d6−1  | 31–40 | 2d6+1  |
| 15–16     | 1d6    | 41–50 | 3d6+1  |

### Defending and Dodging

Spending your action to defend or dodge makes you harder to hit: it adds **+4
to your Target Number** against the relevant attacks for the rest of the turn.

| Action | Usable By  | Defends Against            | Effect                 |
| ------ | ---------- | -------------------------- | ---------------------- |
| Dodge  | Disengaged | Missiles and thrown only   | +4 to your Target Number |
| Defend | Engaged    | Melee and non-missile only | +4 to your Target Number |

### Forced Retreat

If you dealt physical hits and took none:
1. Push enemy back 1 hex in any direction
2. Choose to advance into vacated hex or stand still
3. No retreat hex → enemy rolls 3d6 ≤ DEX or falls

<a id="page-public-rules-combat-action-options-hand-to-hand-and-grappling"></a>

## Hand-to-Hand & Grappling

Fighting bare-handed and grappling are both **Hand-to-Hand (HTH)** actions —
they only happen once you and an enemy share the tight, in-close range HTH
requires. This page covers unarmed strikes, initiating and resisting a
grapple, and how armour changes both. For the conditions that put you in
HTH range in the first place, and the base bare-handed damage table, see
[Special Combat Situations](../special-combat-situations).

### Entering Hand-to-Hand

You may move into an enemy's hex — the HTH option `o` **ATTEMPT HTH** from
[Action Options](../../action-options) — only if one of these holds: the
enemy has their back to a wall, is down/prone/kneeling, has a lower
movement modifier than you, you're attacking from their rear, or they
simply agree. Once you're sharing a hex, **both combatants get +4** to
their to-hit rolls (see [DEX Adjustments](../dex-adjustments)) — grappling
range cuts both ways.

### Unarmed Strikes

An unarmed strike (HTH option `t`, bare hands) uses the normal
[Attack Roll](../attack-rolls): `d20 + to-hit bonus ≥ Target Number`.

- **To-hit bonus:** your DEX combat modifier, the HTH +4, and any
  situational modifiers — same formula as any other attack. No Weapon
  skill applies; there is no bare-hands entry in the skill catalog; if you
  drew a dagger first (option `u`), use its own Weapon skill instead.
- **Target Number:** bare hands resolve on the **Striking** row of the
  [Target Number matrix](../attack-rolls#base-target-number-matrix) — the
  closest published class to a punch or a grab-and-strike. A shield still
  adds its usual TN bonus against an incoming punch; it's a physical
  object in the way regardless of what's swinging.
- **Damage:** use the [Bare-Handed Damage by
  STR](../special-combat-situations#bare-handed-damage-by-str) table, then
  subtract the target's armour `stops` exactly as in the normal damage
  formula. Against a Striking TN of 13–18, most unarmed strikes land; against
  Heavy armour's stops, most of them do nothing.
- **Naturals:** the usual [Natural Rolls](../attack-rolls#natural-rolls)
  apply — a natural 20 still confirms for a severe crit, a natural 1 still
  fumbles. Read "weapon takes stress" on the fumble table as "you jam or
  wrench something" — no weapon to break.

### Initiating a Grapple

Grappling is a separate HTH option: instead of striking, you attempt to
seize and hold the enemy. Make the same attack roll as an unarmed strike,
but check it against the **Flexible/Snare** row of the Target Number
matrix instead of Striking — grabbing and controlling a body is a control
technique, not a blow, and the matrix already prices control techniques as
"poor vs. anything rigid." A hit grapples the target instead of dealing
damage; no damage dice are rolled.

**Armour interaction:** this is where armour matters most. Flexible/Snare
TN runs 13 (unarmoured) → 16 (Light) → 19 (Medium) → 22 (Heavy) — a target
in plate is nearly ungrabbable (a 22 needs a natural 20, same as a dagger
against plate). Leather and cloth barely slow a grapple down; chainmail and
plate are real protection against it. A shield adds its normal TN bonus
here too — you can't close a grip around someone who's got a shield
between you.

**Naturals:** a natural 20 grapples automatically and the target is
briefly stunned — off-balance (−2 to their next action), no separate
confirm roll (there's no damage to double). A natural 1 fumbles: roll 1d6
on the usual [fumble table](../attack-rolls#natural-rolls), reading "drop
weapon" as "you overextend and end up prone" and "weapon takes stress" as
"off-balance instead" — there's no weapon to lose or break.

### Being Grappled

While grappled, you are held in your attacker's hex and your options
shrink to three, chosen in the Actions phase like anything else:

- **Struggle Free** — see [Escaping](#escaping), below.
- **Strike Back** — a normal unarmed strike (or dagger, if already drawn)
  against your captor, at the same HTH +4 both of you already have. A
  grappled hand can still throw an elbow or a headbutt.
- **Hold still** — do nothing and eat whatever your captor does next.

What you **cannot** do: move independently (Phases 3–4 below), ready a new
weapon or swap to one that needs a free hand, fire a missile weapon, gain
any benefit from a shield, or Dodge/Defend. Spellcasting is limited to a
spell you can cast with no hand gestures and no verbal component — Spell
Mastery level 2 and 3 respectively (see [Spell Mastery](../../../magic/spell-mastery)) — since one or both hands are occupied holding on or being held.

The grappler, meanwhile, chooses each turn between:

- **Maintain** — keep the hold; nothing else happens this turn.
- **Squeeze** — a bare-handed strike against the held target, using the
  same Bare-Handed Damage table and armour `stops` as any unarmed strike.
  The target gets no Dodge/Defend bonus against it — they're already held.
- **Release** — a free action that ends the grapple immediately.

### Escaping

Struggling free uses the same roll as a plain HTH [Disengage](../special-combat-situations#disengaging)
(option `v`) — **roll 4d6 ≤ effective DEX** — success stands you up and
moves you to an adjacent empty hex; failure leaves you held. Heavy armour's
DEX penalty is already baked into effective DEX, so the same armour that
made you hard to grab in the first place also makes you slower to break
free of one — there's no separate penalty to track.

### The Six-Phase Turn

Grappling doesn't add phases; it changes what happens inside the existing
[six phases](../../turn-sequence):

| Phase | What changes for a grapple |
| ----- | --------------------------- |
| 1. Initiative | Rolled normally by both combatants — it decides action order in Phase 5, not whether the grapple holds. |
| 2. Renew Spells | A grappled caster can only renew a spell that needs no gestures (Spell Mastery 2+); anything else lapses. |
| 3. Initial Movement | Neither combatant moves — both are locked to the shared hex until the grapple ends. |
| 4. Final Movement | Same as above — a grapple has no movement to yield or take. |
| 5. Actions | Grapple, Strike, Squeeze, Struggle Free, Strike Back, Hold Still, and Release are all resolved here, in adjDEX order, with the HTH +4 applying to both sides. |
| 6. Forced Retreat | Not available against — or to — a grappled figure; there's no hex to push someone into while you're holding them. Retreat becomes available again the turn after the grapple ends. |

<a id="page-public-rules-equipment"></a>

## Equipment

### Currency System

MU (Monetary Unit) is the standard measure of value. In most regions, 1 MU = 1 gold piece (gp).

- 1 MU (e.g. gp) = 10 Lesser MU (e.g. silver pieces (sp))
- 1 Lesser MU (e.g. sp) = 10 Minor MU (e.g. copper pieces (cp))

### Economic Context

- **Poverty line**: 10 gp/month (barely surviving)
- **Decent living**: 100 gp/month (comfortable middle class)
- **Daily survival**: ~0.3 gp/day (3 silver pieces)
- **Comfortable daily**: ~3 gp/day
